source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A near miss confirms that existing safety controls are adequate, so additional review can distort performance data.","B":"Reporting the near miss can reveal contributing factors and system weaknesses before a similar event causes patient harm.","C":"Near misses are useful mainly for identifying which individual should be disciplined when no patient harm occurred.","D":"Safety reporting should be limited to events that cause injury because no learning can come from intercepted errors."}}
source_row.rationale: AHRQ defines a near miss as an error that could have caused harm under different circumstances but was intercepted or did not harm the patient. Patient-safety reporting systems collect near misses so they can be analyzed along with other safety events and used to identify contributing factors and improvement opportunities.
source_row.source_detail: Near misses are reportable safety events and can be analyzed for contributing factors Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15.
